title: Building Gentlemen at Home: How Manners Form Character
author: Martin, Chris
source: The Ways of a Gentleman, February 5, 2026
summary: Manners are not superficial social conventions—they are the external expression of internal respect and consideration. Teaching children good manners teaches them to think of others before themselves, to restrain their impulses, and to value the dignity of those around them. Manners create the friction that prevents selfishness from running unchecked. A parent who prioritizes teaching manners is teaching virtue. The child who must say please and thank you, who must sit up straight and listen, who must consider how his behavior affects others, is learning self-discipline, deference, and the humility that precedes wisdom. Good manners are the training ground of character.
points: Manners teach children to prioritize the dignity and comfort of others over their own impulses.
The discipline of good manners develops self-restraint and consideration that become the foundation of virtue.
Parents who insist on proper manners are actually teaching children essential character traits.
Good manners in childhood create the habits that produce honorable men and women in adulthood.
